# Sombra

Post-quantum privacy on Solana. Private trading and transfers, built for the
quantum era.

Sombra brings quantum-safe privacy to Solana - private UTXO transfers and
shielded trading. Ownership is proven via zero-knowledge proofs of knowledge,
not digital signatures. Transactions are signature-free.

- Website: https://sombra.tech
- Whitepaper: https://sombra.tech/whitepaper.pdf
- Publisher: Bonsol Labs (https://bonsol.org)
- Launch: Mainnet beta, Q2 2026
- Twitter/X: https://x.com/bonsol_labs
- Telegram: https://t.me/+l2s8ejQ170U2ZDUx

---

## What Sombra does

### 01 / Privacy - Your positions, unseen.

Shielded balances and transfers. Front-running bots, on-chain sleuths, and
strangers all see the same thing: nothing.

### 02 / Solana - Solana native.

Private transfers settle in seconds. No bridges to trust, no wrapped tokens to
hold - Sombra is just Solana with a privacy layer.

### 03 / Post-quantum - Built for the next era.

Lattices, not elliptic curves. Hard to break - today and after.

---

## How it works - One UTXO. Three moments.

### 01. Encrypt (ChaCha20-Poly1305 / Kyber-768)

Your payload is wrapped in authenticated encryption, keyed by a Kyber-768
shared secret. One-time use, per UTXO. Only the receiver can read it.

### 02. Prove (RISC0 STARK, ~1.8-2s on RTX 3090)

A RISC0 zkVM proves you own the inputs and the values balance - without
revealing them. STARKs are hash-based, so the proof itself stays hard under
quantum attack.

### 03. Transact (Solana L1, attestation quorum)

The proof and ciphertext land on Solana. Attesting nodes verify and commit a
finalization vote. Ownership is never signed - only proven.

---

## Harvest now, decrypt later

Adversaries are harvesting encrypted traffic today, waiting for tomorrow's
quantum computers to run Shor's algorithm and break elliptic-curve keys.
Sombra ships NIST-standardized lattice cryptography right now - Kyber-768 for
key exchange, RISC0 STARKs for ownership proofs. No elliptic curves to break,
no signatures to forge.

### Cryptographic stack

- Key exchange: ML-KEM-768 (NIST-standardized Kyber-768)
- Encryption: ChaCha20-Poly1305
- Proof system: RISC0 STARK
- GPU proof time: ~2 seconds on RTX 3090

---

## Comparison: Sombra vs Tornado vs Zcash

| Property          | Sombra              | Tornado             | Zcash                 |
|-------------------|---------------------|---------------------|-----------------------|
| Quantum-safe      | Kyber-768           | No - ECC            | No - ECC              |
| No nullifiers     | Yes                 | No                  | No                    |
| Signature-free    | Yes                 | No                  | No                    |
| Proof system      | STARK               | SNARK (ECC)         | SNARK (ECC)           |
| Multi-token       | Any SPL token       | Fixed denominations | ZEC only              |
| Amount privacy    | Yes - per-UTXO      | Fixed only          | Yes - shielded pool   |

Key differentiators:

- Sombra is the only post-quantum privacy protocol on Solana
- Sombra uses per-UTXO amount privacy, distinct from Zcash's shielded pool
- Sombra's ownership is proven via ZK, not signed - removes an entire attack class
- Sombra has no nullifier set, avoiding the scaling and privacy issues of
  nullifier-based schemes

---

## Glossary

- **Kyber-768** - NIST-standardized post-quantum key encapsulation mechanism.
  1184-byte public keys, 1088-byte ciphertexts. Used by Sombra to derive a
  shared secret with the receiver.
- **ML-KEM** - Module Lattice-based Key Encapsulation Mechanism. The NIST FIPS
  203 standard name for the algorithm standardized from Kyber.
- **ChaCha20-Poly1305** - Authenticated encryption with associated data
  (AEAD). Used to encrypt the UTXO payload after Kyber KEM derives a key.
- **RISC0 STARK** - Zero-knowledge proof system that runs a RISC-V virtual
  machine inside a STARK prover. Hash-based, so quantum-resistant. Sombra uses
  RISC0 to prove transaction validity without revealing inputs.
- **STARK** - Scalable Transparent ARgument of Knowledge. A zero-knowledge
  proof system based on hash functions (no trusted setup, no elliptic curves).
- **UTXO** - Unspent Transaction Output. Sombra uses a UTXO model (like
  Bitcoin) rather than account balances (like Ethereum) to enable per-output
  privacy.
- **Signature-free** - Sombra transactions prove ownership via a
  zero-knowledge proof of knowledge of a Kyber secret key, rather than by
  signing with a private key. This removes classical signature attack surfaces
  and is quantum-resistant.
- **No nullifiers** - Sombra does not use a nullifier set to prevent
  double-spending. Instead, UTXO chain validity is enforced by the ZK proof
  itself. This avoids the storage and privacy tradeoffs of nullifier-based
  schemes.
- **Attestation quorum** - A threshold of registered Sombra nodes that verify
  the STARK proof off-chain and submit an attestation vote on-chain. The
  Solana program finalizes the transaction once quorum is reached.

## Key constants (for technical integrators)

- Kyber public key: 1184 bytes
- Kyber ciphertext: 1088 bytes
- AEAD nonce: 12 bytes
- Max UTXO payload: 2048 bytes
- Max tokens per UTXO: 50
- Proof system: RISC0 zkVM 3.0.4
- Target chain: Solana mainnet (Q2 2026 beta)
